transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-05 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~46 minutes | Meeting ID: fir-2025-12-05-nimbus-marketplace-techsync-0321
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Leah Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (Redwood Partnerships), Oliver James (Nimbus Head of Partnerships), Priya Kumar (Nimbus Platform Engineer), Diego Morales (Nimbus Solutions Architect), Hannah Lee (Nimbus PM)

Summary (auto): Quick technical sync to align on the marketplace listing steps, the reference architecture for customers who will buy via Nimbus marketplace, and the cut of joint runbooks. Action items at end.

[00:00] Samir: ok hi everyone thanks for making time, um quick intro, i'll let leah kick into the tech bits but high level we're here to nail down the listing requirements for Nimbus marketplace and what the reference arch should look like for customers who want Redwood Dedicated or private deploy via Nimbus.
[00:16] Oliver: thanks samir, yes we want a clear checklist so our sales and ops teams can certify listings quickly. we also want the joint solution to be easy to deploy from our console.
[00:28] Leah: great, i'll share my screen in a sec. first question — do you expect to surface both hosted (api) and dedicated/private offerings on Nimbus, or focus on dedicated/private for marketplace customers?
[00:40] Hannah: we want both but the priority is dedicated/private because most enterprise buyers in our channel require VPC and SSO. hosted api can be a quick add-on listing later.
[00:50] Priya: yeah and from infra perspective we need a reference arch that maps to our managed VPC environments and the way we provision terraform modules.
[01:02] Leah: perfect. our recommendation is to publish a listing with two SKUs: Hosted API (simple) and Dedicated/Private (validated deployment). the dedicated SKU should reference a validated reference architecture doc, helm chart params, and an operator option for air-gapped installs.
[01:20] Diego: operator option sounds good — we run k8s for the majority of customers but some require on-prem package. can your dedicated runtime be deployed as a helm chart or do you prefer an operator?
[01:32] Leah: both are supported. we have a lightweight operator for lifecycle tasks (model bundles, KV cache warmup, scaling) and a helm chart for teams that want more manual control. note that for high throughput configs we recommend the operator + node pool autoscaling.
[01:48] Oliver: when you say KV cache, is that a managed component or part of the runtime? we need to be precise for our docs.
[01:56] Leah: it's part of the runtime — kv cache (we sometimes see it transcribed as K-V cash, ha) — it's local to the inference nodes but we also support cross-node caching via redis for some topologies. for the marketplace reference arch we'll include both recommended topologies: single-region dedicated pool and multi-az with redis bridging.
[02:18] Samir: also calling out security: for marketplace customers we need to show SOC 2 controls, SAML/SSO setup, KMS/HSM integration, and audit logs. Nimbus — what level of compliance evidence do you require on the listing?
[02:32] Oliver: our enterprise buyers typically require SOC 2 Type II and folks ask for encryption at rest with customer-managed keys. so we want a clear statement and a link to the attestation documents.
[02:42] Maya: we can provide SOC 2 docs and a standard KMS integration guide. on KMS we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer HSMs via KMIP for private installs. we'll add a short matrix to the listing.
[02:56] Priya: about SSO — some customers expect us to do the SAML handshake centrally and others want customers to manage IdP directly. what's the recommended approach for the dedicated SKU?
[03:06] Leah: recommended approach is to support IdP-from-customer via SAML for private/dedicated installs; for hosted we support OIDC + SSO via SAML federation. we'll include an IdP attributes table in the RA.
[03:18] Diego: network requirements — can you share a sample ingress/nat configuration? our provisioning needs the exact port and subnet ranges to open.
[03:26] Leah: yes sample manifests will include ingress, service cidr, and required egress rules. we'll attach a terraform module example too.
[03:33] Samir: quick note on billing/entitlement — Nimbus, do you want us to integrate metering into your licensing so customers purchase Redwood capacity via your marketplace?
[03:42] Oliver: yes ideally metered via your usage API so we can reconcile billing. we also support our own entitlement tokens if you need them for marketplace enablement.
[03:52] Leah: we have a usage endpoint for token-level billing and a marketplace connector pattern we've used with other partners (example: see link to previous listing). we'll share the connector pattern doc.
[04:03] Priya: is there any special network peering we need for the dedicated running in our region? some customers want cross-account VPC peering.
[04:11] Leah: we support VPC peering and PrivateLink style setups depending on cloud. will add recommended patterns per cloud in RA.
[04:19] Hannah: what's the timeline from listing approval to a customer being able to instantiate the bundle?
[04:26] Samir: depends on customer complexity — for standard dedicated with our operator we've seen customers up in 2-3 days; for private on-prem it's usually 2-4 weeks because of network and security reviews.
[04:36] Oliver: ok good to capture that range on the listing.
[04:40] [04:40] Leah: moving on — integration pieces we'd like from Nimbus: a test tenant + sample manifests, a clear artifact upload path for your marketplace (images, chart repo), and a sandbox buying flow so we can smoke test entitlement behavior.
[04:55] Priya: we can spin up a tenant and provide a chart repo entry. i'll confirm repo credentials after the call.
[05:02] Diego: on support model — who handles first-line for infra issues vs model quality issues? if marketplace customers buy from Nimbus, do we send them to Nimbus support first?
[05:12] Maya: recommended flow: Nimbus handles marketplace onboarding and billing support, Redwood handles runtime and model quality issues. we'll provide a runbook for triage and an escalation matrix.
[05:21] Hannah: do you have SLAs for latency/availability for Dedicated? we need numbers to show in our marketplace listing.
[05:29] Leah: yes we provide options: Gold SLA (99.95% uptime target, latency p50/p95 targets per model) for reserved capacity; Standard SLA for burstable. exact numbers will be in the listing with a note on benchmark variance by model and sequence length.
[05:45] Oliver: can we include a small benchmark artifact for a representative model so buyers can see latency/cost tradeoffs on the listing?
[05:52] Samir: yes we'll include a benchmark snapshot and link to our public perf profiles. we'll add a 'typical configs' table showing cost per 1M tokens for different setups.
[06:02] Priya: any concerns about secrets management? customers expect keys not to be stored on Nimbus side.
[06:10] Leah: we support customer-managed keys and don't store plaintext keys in our control plane for private installs. for marketplace connector we'll set up secure artifact exchange and short-lived creds.
[06:20] Diego: about packaging — we prefer a single listing that references two deployment options; is that ok?
[06:26] Samir: yes a single listing with SKUs/variants is ideal. we'll provide copy and recommended tile images for your UI.
[06:33] [06:33] Oliver: is there any legal doc we should attach up-front (purchasing terms, DPA)?
[06:38] Maya: we'll provide standard DPA and terms for marketplace transactions. if Nimbus requires additional language we can iterate with your legal team.
[06:46] Priya: micro question — do you support GPU selection and quantization profiles in the helm chart? we need to pin instance types.
[06:54] Leah: yes the helm chart exposes instance profile/quantization presets; we'll include recommended presets for CPU vs GPU vs quantized int8 workloads.
[07:03] Hannah: for the RA diagram can you include a failure mode section? buyers like to see how the system degrades under capacity pressure.
[07:11] Leah: absolutely — we'll add graceful degradation patterns: fallback to smaller model variant, retry/backoff, and cross-region failover.
[07:20] Diego: on metrics — what do you expose for ops: per-token cost, request rate, latency histograms?
[07:26] Leah: we expose token-level counters, token cost breakdowns, latency percentiles per route, KV cache hit rates, and per-model throughput. we also provide tracing hooks for integration with your observability.
[07:38] Priya: ok good. we'll need to know retention policy for traces and logs for compliance.
[07:44] Maya: default logs retained 30 days; we can provide extended retention as an add-on. traces can be forwarded to customer observability endpoints.
[07:53] Oliver: anything else on the technical side?
[07:56] Samir: quick recap of deliverables — Samir share listing template and perf snippet, Leah RA + helm params + runbook, Priya provide test tenant + manifests, Diego confirm SAML attributes. schedule pilot once test tenant ready.
[08:12] Priya: i'll also attach an example terraform module we use for provisioning.
[08:16] Diego: will do the IdP details after the call.
[08:19] [08:19] Samir: great. any blockers?
[08:21] Oliver: none on our side. looking forward to the RA and the pilot.
[08:25] [08:25] Leah: one small technical caveat — for customers with heavy concurrency we recommend pre-warmed KV cache and reserved capacity; otherwise latency spikes on cold start. we'll document warmup scripts.
[08:38] Priya: do you have a recommended warmup pattern?
[08:40] Leah: yes we have a small warmup utility and a sample job that runs a set of canonical prompts to populate the kv cache and model weights. we'll include it in the runbook.
[08:50] Oliver: ok perfect.
[08:52] Maya: i'll follow up on legal intro if needed.
[08:55] Samir: thanks everyone. we'll send the docs and set up a follow-up 30 minute pilot kickoff once test tenant is available.
[09:03] End transcript.
